fruit: Pears from the river farms, crisp and cold!
Jujubes, dried jujubes, good for the blood!
Melons! Cut fresh, a copper a slice!
Plums, black and sweet! Come and taste!
Grapes from Dunhuang, carried by camel!
silk: Feel this, traveller: softer than a cloud!
Red silk for weddings, blue for scholars!
Bolts of silk, cut to your length!
Embroidered sashes, every one by hand!
Silk that crossed the desert twice!
buns: Sweet bean buns, two for a copper!
Steamed rolls, soft as a pillow!
tea: Green tea from the southern hills!
A cup of jasmine for the dust of the road!
Hot tea, cold days, good company!
Sit, sit, the kettle is singing!
iron: Pots and pans, beaten not cast!
A blade for the bandit road?
Hoes and sickles for the harvest!
herbs: Licorice root, sweet for the throat!
Wolfberries, for the eyes and the heart!
Ginger for the cold, mint for the heat!
Dried mushrooms from the tiger slopes!
pottery: Bowls and jars, fired this week!
Glazed cups, blue as the sky!
Teapots from the kilns of the east!
Clay for the kitchen, glaze for the guest!
spice: Star anise, a pinch makes the pot!
Saffron, worth its weight in silver!

walker: Off to see my cousin by the east gate.
chatter: And then he said the price had doubled!
My son joined the army last spring.
Did you hear the bell this morning?
The tea house has a new singer.
Rain by evening, mark my words.
sitter: Ah, my old legs thank this bench.
Sit a while, the day is long.
I have watched this square for forty years.
porter: One more trip and I can rest.
Careful, this crate is from Dunhuang.
The horse knows the way better than I do.
child: I saw a tiger once! A small one.
Mother says not to talk to strangers.
guard: Keep your weapon sheathed inside the walls.
Report anything strange to the gate.
vendor: Come back tomorrow, more goods arrive.
worker: Hot iron waits for no one.
The master wants these done by dusk.

rumours.text: They say the Seal is gone from the temple.
Ghosts in the southern grass, my neighbour swears it.
Lanterns drowned in the swamp, and still they glow.
The old tombs are restless. Nobody goes near them now.
Bandits on the road again. The silk carts go with guards.
Tigers on the south slopes again, bold as you like.
A woman rides a blue tiger in the hills, they say.
The smith is casting a bell. A bell! For a tiger!
